summary: Tracing no longer hand-spells the GenAI/Langfuse dialect — every model call now traces through strands.telemetry, and the debrief/standing fold stopped producing two overlapping traces per call.
details: nora/obs/tracing.py's generation()/annotate_generation() (a hand-rolled langfuse.observation.*/gen_ai.* dialect) are deleted. A new nora/agent/telemetry.py — the only module besides nora/agent/structured.py allowed to import strands — owns provider/exporter setup (setup_agent_tracing, wiring Nora's own R-76 sampler through strands.telemetry.StrandsTelemetry) and the span pair a raw chat.completions.create call needs (start_raw_model_span/end_raw_model_span, thin wrappers around Strands' own Tracer.start_model_invoke_span/end_model_invoke_span). Both guard their own bodies (never load-bearing, matching nora.obs.tracing.span's own rule) so a broken tracer cannot turn into a discarded model verdict.

The debrief fold and standing fold (via nora.agent.structured.ask_text) have run through a real Strands Agent since an earlier change (4448c737), but the hand-rolled generation() wrapper around that call was never removed — so every fold/consolidate/verdict call produced two nested, overlapping traces: the wrapper span and Strands' own automatic agent+model-invoke spans underneath it. This is the concrete shape behind reports of 10+ separate traces per message in Langfuse. The wrapper is deleted; ask_text gained a trace_attributes parameter so tag_id/conversation_id/a call label still reach the Strands-produced span.

The relevance gate's raw call (the one path that must stay off the Agent SDK — its verdict-formation mechanism is unchanged and still pinned by tests/architecture/test_the_gate_does_not_form_its_verdict_through_the_sdk.py) now opens/closes through the new start_raw_model_span/end_raw_model_span pair instead of the retired helper.

nora.infra.vision.client's raw call gets no span of its own either way — nora.infra sits below both nora.obs and nora.agent in the layered-import contract and cannot reach either. This is a known, pre-existing gap (a vision read exports zero token usage), not something this change fixes or worsens.
limitations: OPERATOR DECISION, not a side effect: the relevance gate's prompt (every room's transcript, including rooms Nora does not serve) and the debrief/standing fold's prompt/completion now reach the collector unredacted, where both used to be screened or safe-by-construction before this change. design/evaluation/08-the-sdk-surface.md §4.2 had already named the gate's exposure as a fork requiring exactly this tradeoff to close a gap in the evaluation suite's span mapper (40 of 150 cases blocked on it); the operator was told plainly and chose to accept it. design/13-trace-content-and-redaction.md's native Strands redaction lever (off by default) is the one mechanism that would cover both the Agent-backed paths and this raw one at once, since both now go through the same Tracer.

A separate, pre-existing correctness gap was found while correcting stale documentation for this change and is NOT fixed here: nora.agent.structured.ask_text has no catch for Strands' MaxTokensReachedException (which the event loop raises unconditionally on a max-tokens stop reason), unlike the tag turn's own Agent invocation in nora/agent/factory.py, which explicitly catches it. Whether a debrief/standing-fold call that hits the token ceiling is silently mis-counted as a hard error rather than the intended unavailable/length outcome has not been verified live. Predates this session (introduced when 4448c737 moved these calls onto ask_text); recorded rather than fixed.
